exec.description: Executable for the event-reaction role. Relative paths resolve against the plugin dir; bare names resolve on PATH.

subscribes.description: Bus events forwarded to exec's stdin. ["*"] = all.

runAction.description: Executable invoked request/response (raw {type,config,card} JSON on stdin → result JSON on stdout, bounded by a timeout) when the server dispatches one of this plugin's `catalog.actions` for a patrol. Same path-resolution rules as `exec` (relative paths resolve against the plugin dir; bare names resolve on PATH). Distinct from `exec`, which is long-lived for the event-reaction role.

optionsExec.description: Executable invoked request/response (raw {field,search?} JSON on stdin → [{value,label}] JSON on stdout, bounded by a timeout) to populate a config field marked `dynamic: true` (e.g. a GitLab project picker fetched live from the API). Same path-resolution rules as `exec`. Dispatched by the server's `connector_options` rpc.

config.description: User-supplied settings, rendered as a form in the app. Each field's `key` is referenced by `webhooks` (urlFrom/secretFrom) and injected as an env var into any `exec`.

webhooks.description: Webhook transport handled by the server core. Outbound POSTs on bus events; inbound exposes a signed HTTP route. Service specifics are declared here, not coded.

catalog.description: Display metadata for the in-app catalog and the trigger picker: human name, icon, role verbs. Optional; surfaced (opaquely) via list_plugins.

icon.description: Icon id the app maps to a glyph (e.g. mail, slack, github).

verbs.description: User-facing capability tags. `trigger` = surfaces in the Add-Trigger picker.

summary.description: One-line description shown under the trigger in the picker.

config.description: Connector-specific trigger settings (e.g. which GitLab project/events to watch), rendered in the patrol editor's trigger row and stored on the task's eventTrigger.config. Same field shape as catalog.actions[].config.

dynamic.description: For a `select`: fetch the option list live from the connector's `optionsExec` (keyed by this field's `key`) instead of the static `options` array. The app renders a searchable dropdown that still allows a free-typed value.

setup.description: An in-app "Connect" step (e.g. OAuth consent) the server can run on the user's behalf via the `run_plugin_setup` rpc — see PROTOCOL.md's "Role 5".

type.description: Informational — both run the same way (spawn `command`).

command.description: Shell-split argv, e.g. "node connect.mjs". Spawned with cwd = the plugin dir, env = the instance's resolved config.

auth.description: Auth methods this connector offers, rendered as tabs in the connect wizard. Each groups a subset of the `config` fields; a method with `kind: oauth` also shows a Sign in button that runs `catalog.setup`. Fields not claimed by any method (and not `hidden`) render above the tabs as common settings.

kind.description: `oauth` shows a Sign in button (`catalog.setup`); `token` is fields only.

summary.description: One-line hint shown inside the tab.

fields.description: Config field keys shown in this tab. Omit for a method that needs no input (e.g. one-click sign in with a shipped client).

actions.description: Post-run actions this connector can perform (send an email, post a message…). Surfaced in the patrol editor's Actions picker; the config is rendered as a form and passed to the connector's runAction.

id.description: Action type, dispatched to the adapter's actions[id] handler.

dynamic.description: For a `select`: fetch the option list live from the connector's `optionsExec` (keyed by this field's `key`) instead of the static `options` array.

key.description: Identifier; referenced by webhooks and injected as an env var name into exec.

type.description: `secret` values are stored in the OS keychain, never in settings.json or logs.

dynamic.description: For a `select`: fetch the option list live from the connector's `optionsExec` (keyed by this field's `key`) instead of the static `options` array.

hidden.description: Never rendered in the config form — set programmatically (e.g. an OAuth refresh token filled by the Sign in flow).

direction.description: `out` = core POSTs on matching bus events. `in` = core exposes a signed HTTP route.

urlFrom.description: out only — config key whose value is the destination URL.

events.description: out only — card statuses / bus event names that fire this webhook.

action.description: in only — rpc command to dispatch with the mapped payload (e.g. create_card).

map.description: in only — { rpcField: JSONPath } extracted from the inbound body.

exec.description: Optional escape hatch. Core invokes it request/response (raw request JSON on stdin → transformed payload / verify verdict on stdout) when named schemes/mapping don't fit.

scheme.description: Named signature scheme implemented in the core. `gitlab` is a plain constant-time compare against the `X-Gitlab-Token` header (GitLab has no HMAC signature).

header.description: Request header carrying the signature (e.g. X-Hub-Signature-256).

secretFrom.description: Config key whose value is the shared signing secret.
